claims.title: Job messages may be intercepted between the web tier and message queue
claims.description: `flow:process:web-application>store:message-queue>enqueue-job` crosses from the web tier to the backend tier and carries `business-critical-data`, but its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If that unknown resolves to no effective transport encryption, an attacker able to observe this inter-tier path can intercept job messages sent by `process:web-application` to `store:message-queue`. The disclosed jobs may reveal the work later consumed by `process:background-worker-process`; confirm protection for this crossing rather than treating the unknown as plaintext.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the flow crosses a trust boundary and its transport encryption is unstated, although an attacker must obtain observation of that path. Impact is medium because the flow is tagged `business-critical-data` and exposes queued work crossing from `boundary:web-tier` to `boundary:backend-tier`.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and authenticate the web-to-queue connection
mitigations.detail: Set verified TLS, preferably mutual TLS or equivalent service authentication, on `flow:process:web-application>store:message-queue>enqueue-job` and record the resulting `encryption_in_transit` state.

claims.title: Queued job contents may be intercepted by an observer of the worker read path
claims.description: `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:message-queue>consume-job` carries `business-critical-data` between `process:background-worker-process` and `store:message-queue`, while its protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If transport protection is absent or ineffective, an attacker with a foothold able to observe the backend-tier path can intercept job contents as the worker consumes them. Those contents are then used by the worker's downstream database operation on `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:database>read-write-records`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because encryption is unverified but the worker and queue are both in `boundary:backend-tier`, so an attacker needs an internal observation position. Impact is medium because the flow is explicitly tagged `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Require encrypted worker-to-queue transport
mitigations.detail: Configure authenticated TLS for `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:message-queue>consume-job`, including certificate validation on the worker and queue endpoints.

claims.title: Database records may be intercepted on the worker database connection
claims.description: `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:database>read-write-records` carries application records and log records tagged `business-critical-data`, but both its protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the unresolved transport control is absent, an attacker observing the backend-tier connection can intercept records returned from `store:database` to `process:background-worker-process`. The disclosure includes records and logs that the worker handles, without requiring database credentials.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the unverified connection remains inside `boundary:backend-tier` and requires an internal on-path position. Impact is medium because `store:database` and its read-write flow hold application and log records tagged `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Enforce TLS for database connections
mitigations.detail: Use verified TLS for `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:database>read-write-records`, require certificate validation, and document the protocol and transport-encryption settings.

claims.title: Queue credentials may be intercepted while the web application reads configuration
claims.description: `flow:process:web-application>store:web-application-config>read-configuration` carries settings and message-queue credentials from `store:web-application-config`, whose assets include `credentials` and `secrets`. Its protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the configuration read path is not protected in transit, an attacker able to observe it can intercept the queue credential. That credential can then enable later access to `store:message-queue`; this draft does not assume that it does.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the configuration read occurs within `boundary:web-tier` and requires an on-path foothold, while its encryption state is unstated. Impact is high because the flow and `store:web-application-config` carry queue credentials and secrets, which can unlock subsequent service access.

mitigations.summary: Protect configuration retrieval with authenticated TLS
mitigations.detail: Require TLS with endpoint authentication on `flow:process:web-application>store:web-application-config>read-configuration` and prevent credential values from appearing in connection diagnostics.

mitigations.summary: Use short-lived queue credentials
mitigations.detail: Issue narrowly scoped, rotating credentials from a dedicated secret-management service so an intercepted value has limited lifetime and reach.

claims.title: Database credentials may be intercepted while the worker reads configuration
claims.description: `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:worker-config>read-configuration` carries settings and database credentials from `store:worker-config`, which holds `credentials` and `secrets`; its protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If that unknown resolves to an unprotected connection, an internal on-path attacker can intercept the database credential during configuration retrieval. The recovered credential could enable later reads of `store:database`, subject to whatever authentication and authorization that store actually enforces.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because this backend-tier path requires an internal observation position and the encryption state is unverified. Impact is high because the flow carries database credentials from a store tagged `credentials` and `secrets`, potentially enabling further access to `store:database`.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the worker configuration read path
mitigations.detail: Require authenticated TLS and certificate validation for `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:worker-config>read-configuration`.

mitigations.summary: Replace standing database secrets with short-lived identity
mitigations.detail: Use workload identity or dynamically issued, scoped database credentials rather than a reusable credential stored in worker configuration.

claims.title: A queue storage copy may disclose queued work if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:message-queue` holds `business-critical-data` and has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If this unresolved attribute means queued payloads are not encrypted at rest, an attacker who obtains queue storage media or an operational copy can read retained job messages without using the normal worker read path. The disclosure can expose work later handled by `process:background-worker-process`; this is conditional and does not assert that queue encryption is absent.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because storage encryption is unverified and a copied queue volume or operational copy bypasses application access controls. Impact is medium because the queue is tagged `business-critical-data`, although its data classification is also unknown.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce queue encryption at rest
mitigations.detail: Establish the `encryption_at_rest` state for `store:message-queue`, then require managed-key encryption for queue payload persistence and all operational copies, snapshots, and backups.

claims.title: A database storage copy may disclose application and log records if unencrypted
claims.description: `store:database` contains application records and application log records, is tagged `business-critical-data`, and has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If the unknown resolves to no encryption at rest, an attacker holding a database volume, backup, snapshot, or other storage-layer copy can read those records directly, bypassing `process:background-worker-process` and the database's normal authentication path. This remains a conditional finding until the storage protection is verified.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because an unencrypted storage copy would be readable without live database access, but the at-rest control is currently unstated. Impact is medium because the database contains application and log records tagged `business-critical-data`, while its classification is unknown.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt database media and derived copies
mitigations.detail: Verify `store:database` encryption at rest, enforce managed-key encryption on the primary store and backups or snapshots, and restrict export and restore permissions.

mitigations.summary: Minimize sensitive log content
mitigations.detail: Redact credentials and unnecessary record content before application logs are written to `store:database`.

claims.title: A copied web configuration store may reveal queue credentials if unencrypted
claims.description: `store:web-application-config` holds queue credentials and secrets, and its `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If that store or its operational copies are unencrypted, an attacker holding a volume, backup, snapshot, or exported configuration copy can recover the queue credential without accessing `process:web-application`. The recovered secret may enable a later attempt to access `store:message-queue`; the scope of that credential is not stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the configuration store's at-rest protection is unverified and copied storage bypasses its live read path. Impact is high because `store:web-application-config` is tagged `credentials` and `secrets` and is stated to hold the queue credential.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt configuration-store media and backups
mitigations.detail: Verify encryption at rest for `store:web-application-config` and require managed-key encryption and tightly restricted export access for all copies.

mitigations.summary: Move queue credentials to dedicated secret management
mitigations.detail: Use a dedicated secret store with short-lived, rotated queue credentials instead of retaining reusable secrets in general application configuration.

claims.title: A copied worker configuration store may reveal database credentials if unencrypted
claims.description: `store:worker-config` holds database credentials and secrets, but its `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If storage encryption is absent, an attacker obtaining a storage-layer copy can recover the database credential from the configuration store rather than using `process:background-worker-process`. That credential can subsequently be presented to the database, subject to the still-unknown authentication and authorization controls on its normal read path.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because an unencrypted configuration copy would expose its contents without live worker access, though encryption at rest is unverified. Impact is high because `store:worker-config` holds database credentials and secrets that can enable onward access to `store:database`.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt worker configuration at rest
mitigations.detail: Verify and enforce managed-key encryption on `store:worker-config` and every backup, snapshot, or exported copy.

mitigations.summary: Use dynamic database credentials
mitigations.detail: Replace retained database credentials with short-lived workload-issued credentials and rotate any existing stored secret.

claims.title: A compromised worker may read queued jobs if queue reader authentication is weak
claims.description: `process:background-worker-process` reads from `store:message-queue` through `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:message-queue>consume-job`, which is a `read-write` operation carrying `business-critical-data`. Authentication on that flow is unknown. If the queue does not strongly authenticate and narrowly authorize the worker identity, an attacker running in the worker or holding a grant equivalent to it can read queued job contents. The disclosure exposes work submitted by `process:web-application` before or while the worker processes it.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the worker is internal and the attacker must control it or obtain an equivalent queue grant, although authentication is unstated. Impact is medium because the queue read path carries `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate and scope the queue consumer identity
mitigations.detail: Assign `process:background-worker-process` a distinct workload identity limited to consuming only the required queue, and record strong authentication on the consume flow.

claims.title: A compromised worker may read database records if database access is not narrowly authenticated
claims.description: `process:background-worker-process` reads application and log records from `store:database` using `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:database>read-write-records`, whose authentication is unknown. If the database does not require a strongly authenticated, least-privileged worker identity, an attacker controlling the worker or holding an equivalent grant can read the database corpus. This disclosure includes the application's log records as well as application records and bypasses any user-facing request boundary.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the worker is internal and exploitation requires code execution in it or an equivalent database grant; the flow authentication is unknown. Impact is medium because the database contains application and log records tagged `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Apply least-privilege database read access
mitigations.detail: Require a distinct authenticated worker identity for `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:database>read-write-records`, limited to necessary tables, rows, and columns.

mitigations.summary: Restrict log access separately
mitigations.detail: Separate application-log access from operational record access and redact sensitive fields before logs reach `store:database`.

claims.title: Compromise of the internet-facing web application may expose queue credentials
claims.description: `process:web-application` is internet-facing and reads settings and queue credentials from `store:web-application-config` through `flow:process:web-application>store:web-application-config>read-configuration`. Authentication on that read flow is unknown. If access to the configuration store is not limited to a strongly authenticated, narrowly scoped workload identity, an attacker executing in the web application can recover the queue credential from the configuration read path. The credential can then support onward access attempts to `store:message-queue`, depending on the queue's unstated authentication controls.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `process:web-application` is internet-facing and already has a configuration read path, while authentication for that path is unstated. Impact is high because the configuration store holds credentials and secrets, including the queue credential.

mitigations.summary: Use a narrowly scoped workload identity for configuration reads
mitigations.detail: Require `process:web-application` to authenticate to `store:web-application-config` with an identity permitted only to retrieve its own required secret material.

mitigations.summary: Avoid exposing reusable queue credentials to the process
mitigations.detail: Use short-lived, scoped queue access tokens or a secret broker so compromising the web application does not reveal a durable queue credential.

claims.title: A compromised worker may recover database credentials from worker configuration
claims.description: `process:background-worker-process` reads database credentials from `store:worker-config` through `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:worker-config>read-configuration`, whose authentication is unknown. If the configuration store does not enforce a strongly authenticated, least-privileged worker identity, an attacker controlling the worker can recover the database credential. The credential may then be used against `store:database`, where the worker's read-write flow also has unknown authentication.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the attacker must first control the internal `process:background-worker-process`, although both configuration and database-flow authentication are unstated. Impact is high because `store:worker-config` holds database credentials and secrets that may enable subsequent database access.

mitigations.summary: Constrain worker configuration access
mitigations.detail: Require a dedicated worker workload identity, authenticated transport, and least-privilege read authorization for `store:worker-config`.

mitigations.summary: Eliminate durable database credentials from configuration
mitigations.detail: Use dynamically issued, short-lived database credentials and rotate the existing database credential if it has ever been stored in worker configuration.
